transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-11
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Jake Thompson (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Acme Head of Security), Dan Ruiz (Acme Platform), Priya Nair (Acme Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Security posture discovery focused on SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs, encryption and KMS, and data retention policy.
- Acme evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
- Next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, SAML guide, schedule infra POC call, share Dedicated pricing/size.

Transcript: (timestamps approx every 20-45s, transcription imperfect)
[00:00] Jake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jake Thompson from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Maya our solutions engineer.
[00:07] Maya: hi all, thanks for making time. we'll keep it focused on security posture stuff today.
[00:12] Laura: Great thanks. I'm Laura, head of security at Acme. Dan and Priya are here as well.
[00:17] Dan: hi.
[00:18] Priya: hello.
[00:20] Jake: quick agenda — SOC2/ISO and attestation, SSO and SAML, RBAC and audit logs, encryption and KMS, retention and deletion policies, and then any legal/compliance asks. Sound good?
[00:29] Laura: yes. We are evaluating between hosted and dedicated; there are some regs that push us to private if we can't get certain controls.
[00:36] Maya: understood. maybe I'll start with what we can provide on hosted: we are SOC2 Type II audited, and have an ISO 27001 scope — we'll share the actual reports after the call but high level we cover infrastructure, app controls, change management.
[00:48] Laura: do you have the specific date range for the latest SOC2? we need the period for our audit tracking.
[00:53] Jake: latest SOC2 Type II covers Jan-Dec 2024. we'll attach the PDF.
[00:58] [00:58] Priya: and the ISO cert?
[01:02] Maya: ISO 27001 certificate active as of 2024 Q3, scope doc included in the packet.
[01:08] Laura: ok good. on SSO, we run SAML 2.0 and onelogin for IdP, do you support that?
[01:14] Maya: yes, SAML 2.0 supported. we have docs and a short metadata exchange flow. we also support SCIM for user provisioning, though SCIM options depend on deployment mode — hosted supports SCIM, Dedicated also, Private can integrate with customer IdP via VPC.
[01:28] Dan: when you say Private, do you mean full on-prem or VPC peering? what are the network options?
[01:33] Jake: both. Private can be VPC-hosted in your cloud with customer-managed networking, or an on-prem package for air-gapped. networking options include VPC peering, PrivateLink (cloud-providers), and IP allowlists. we'll confirm region availability.
[01:45] [01:45] Laura: encryption at rest — what KMS options? can we bring our own keys?
[01:50] Maya: short answer: yes for Dedicated and Private — BYOK via customer KMS is supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For hosted we use our managed KMS by default but we do offer a dedicated tenant option that can be configured with customer-managed keys for enterprise contracts.
[02:07] Dan: is there HSM support or only software KMS?
[02:10] Maya: we integrate with cloud HSM-backed KMS providers; if you need an on-prem HSM we can work through the Private on-prem deployment.
[02:19] Laura: audit logs are critical. do you provide immutable audit trails and retention controls?
[02:24] Maya: yes, we produce audit logs for admin actions, model deploys, API keys and token usage. logs can be exported to customer SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, S3) and for Dedicated/Private we can push into your logging pipeline. retention controls configurable per plan; hosted default retention is 90 days but we offer longer retention as add-on.
[02:45] Priya: for legal we need to see how long PII or prompts are retained. Do you store user prompts permanently?
[02:52] Jake: by default hosted stores logs/prompts for 30-90 days for quality monitoring and abuse prevention; we have explicit options for data retention and deletion under enterprise agreements. Private deployments give you full control since data stays in your VPC/on-prem.
[03:07] Laura: can you do automatic purge and do you support a data deletion API?
[03:11] Maya: yes, deletion API exists and we can run a scrub on request. For Hosted we provide deletion workflows and a data processing addendum that defines deletion timelines and attestations.
[03:22] Dan: what about tokenization or redaction for PII before it hits model? any pre-ingest processing?
[03:27] Maya: we have optional pre-processing pipeline that can mask or hash fields; you can run filters client-side or use our edge transformations in Dedicated/Private. we'll share a short tech note on pre-ingest redaction.
[03:39] Laura: RBAC — can we map native roles to our IdP groups and have granular permissions for model deploy, route creation, and cost visibility?
[03:48] Maya: yes, RBAC integrates with SAML/SCIM groups. we have built-in roles (admin, dev, viewer) and fine-grained permissions for model deploys, rollouts, and access to logs/cost dashboards. For Private we can add custom roles.
[04:00] [04:00] Priya: any SOC controls around privileged access and key rotation?
[04:05] Maya: privileged ops access is logged and requires MFA; we rotate keys internally on a schedule and recommend customer-managed key rotation via their KMS. we can provide control mappings to SOC trust services criteria.
[04:18] Laura: we also need to understand your incident response and breach notification SLAs.
[04:22] Jake: incident response runs through our security team; we have a 72-hour notification standard for confirmed breaches to customers and can add faster notifications per contract. we'll share the IR plan summary.
[04:33] Dan: performance: if we go Dedicated to meet latency and residency, how do rollouts work? can we pin versions and do canaries?
[04:39] Maya: you can pin model versions, do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and set automatic fallback policies. these are in the Redwood Console and work the same across hosted/dedicated/private. we'll demo that in the next session.
[04:52] Laura: for compliance we need continuous monitoring evidence — do you have monitoring exports or attestations we can ingest?
[04:58] Maya: yes exports, metrics, tracer logs; we can provide read-only monitoring views for auditors and periodic attestations.
[05:07] Priya: on contractual terms — data residency and subprocessing — do you have a standard DPA?
[05:12] Jake: yes we have a DPA and standard subprocessor list; we'll provide both. for residency we can restrict hosting regions for hosted enterprise customers and Dedicated/Private gives full control.
[05:25] Laura: any nuances in support levels and SLA targets for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[05:29] Maya: hosted has baseline SLOs; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets—details differ by commitment tier. we'll share the exact SLA doc.
[05:39] Dan: encryption in transit — TLS versions supported? FIPS?
[05:42] Maya: TLS 1.2+ supported, TLS 1.3 on by default. FIPS endpoints available for Dedicated/Private if required; we'll note that.
[05:52] Laura: for audit logs, can logs be certified tamper-evident? do you support append-only storage?
[05:58] Maya: for Dedicated/Private we can push logs to your append-only S3 bucket with object lock, or we can integrate with immutable logging systems. hosted default uses managed logging; we have attestations around log integrity.
[06:12] [06:12] Jake: switching gears quick, do you have timeline constraints for this evaluation?
[06:16] Laura: we'd like to choose a vendor by end of Q2. there are two internal milestones: security review completion in 4 weeks and a pilot in mid-April.
[06:26] Jake: good. for the pilot do you expect to run it in hosted or Dedicated?
[06:30] Dan: we'd prefer to start hosted but need to test Dedicated for latency/residency — so maybe a two-track pilot.
[06:37] Maya: that's common — we can set up a lightweight hosted pilot for feature validation and a Dedicated sizing/benchmark window for perf. we'll put together a plan.
[06:47] Priya: on legal, specific export controls and data flow mapping — we will need a vendor security questionnaire answered.
[06:55] Jake: we have a security questionnaire template and can fill in standard sections; we'll also provide our SOC2 and ISO docs to speed things up.
[07:05] Laura: a few nitty-gritty Qs: do you store model weights or any preloaded prompts that could be considered sensitive across tenants?
[07:12] Maya: model artifacts reside in storage controlled by Redwood; for multi-tenant hosted models the models are shared but weights are not modifiable per tenant. for Dedicated/Private you can host model artifacts in your tenant and we can support pinning a specific model binary.
[07:27] Dan: do you do any centralized telemetry that contains prompt contents for usage analytics?
[07:32] Maya: telemetry captures metadata and token counts; for prompts we store them only when retention is enabled for quality/monitoring. we can disable that or route telemetry to your logging in Dedicated/Private.
[07:45] [07:45] Priya: how do you handle subpoenas or legal requests for data?
[07:49] Jake: we notify customers per the DPA and provide assistance; for Private deployments customer control gives you custody of data, for Hosted we follow legal process and notify. details in the DPA and standard TOS exceptions.
[07:59] Laura: any certifications beyond SOC2/ISO? FedRAMP? HIPAA?
[08:04] Maya: we are working towards HIPAA readiness and have a HIPAA addendum option; FedRAMP not currently. if FedRAMP is a blocker we can discuss partners.
[08:14] Dan: about key management — can we rotate keys frequently without downtime?
[08:18] Maya: yes we support key rotation patterns via KMS; for BYOK we recommend rotating keys in KMS with a short overlap window and Redwood supports key rewrap to avoid downtime.
[08:29] Priya: will you provide control mappings (e.g., mapping Redwood controls to our SOC checklist) so our audit team can sign off?
[08:34] Jake: yes, we can provide a control mapping matrix and a runbook for auditors.
[08:40] Maya: I'll add that to the packet we send after the call.
[08:44] [08:44] Laura: ok this is helpful. any cost delta we should be aware of for the Dedicated/Private choices?
[08:49] Jake: Dedicated has a higher base cost due to reserved capacity; Private/on-prem is custom pricing. we'll include a pricing worksheet.
[08:57] Dan: can we run a small benchmark — e.g., 2 model endpoints with 100 concurrent requests — to test latency?
[09:02] Maya: yes we can run a benchmark plan. for Dedicated we can provision a small pool and run load tests; for hosted we'll run a performance test under a hosted tenant.
[09:13] Priya: any safety/compliance tooling around content filtering and model hallucination monitoring?
[09:18] Maya: we have policy engines, custom filter rules, and quality eval hooks that can trigger regression alerts. we'll include docs and examples.
[09:27] Jake: wrapping up, recap of next steps: Jake to send SOC2/ISO and DPA, Maya to send SAML/SCIM integration guide, control mapping, and SSO metadata, and schedule follow-up POC planning call. Acme to provide KMS/hsm requirements and desired retention policy.
[09:45] Laura: sounds right. we'll aim for security review signoff in 4 weeks.
[09:49] Jake: great — thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for the POC planning session.
[09:55] Dan: thanks.
[09:56] Priya: thanks everyone.
[09:57] Maya: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
